messages:
maria (Support): FYI incoming escalation from AcmeHealth — they rotated an API key via the Console ~12:20 UTC and now a subset of requests routed through our EU-edge proxies are getting 401 and intermittent connection errors. Customer reports spike in errors right after rotation and some clients retrying see 503s. They need a mitigation path ASAP.
ken (Infra): Can you paste the exact error samples and the rotation method? self-serve UI, API, or vault CLI? Also which model/service they call (generation vs embeddings)?
maria (Support): They used the Console -> API keys -> rotate button. Calls are to /v1/generate (hosted). Attached logs from their side:

```
2026-03-14T12:21:05Z ERROR request id=xyz path=/v1/generate status=401 msg=\"invalid api key\"
2026-03-14T12:21:06Z WARN retry attempt=1 upstream=http://eu-edge-3.example.net conn_err=\"connection refused\"
2026-03-14T12:21:07Z ERROR request id=abc path=/v1/generate status=503 msg=\"upstream_unavailable\"
```

maria (Support): They also sent our proxy logs showing repeated `x-api-key` on the wire matching the new key, but header `x-key-id` still shows old key id in some requests. Looks like split brain between edge cache and control plane.
jason (Eng): Hmm — rotation flow should rotate in control plane, push a short-lived token to edge caches, and then replace long-lived secret in KMS/Vault. If some proxies still have old `key-id` cached while clients are sending new secret we could see auth failures where our auth service expects key-id+signature to match.
ben (SRE): I'm pulling edge proxy metrics. There's a deployment to eu-edge cluster that rolled at 12:10 UTC yesterday. Could be stale sticky connections to a pre-rotation envoy.
\\
ben (SRE): Quick check: the edge auth cache TTL is 5m and we also publish an invalidation event on rotation. @deploy-bot can you show the rotation event logs for key id `ak_live_...` around 12:20?
deploy-bot: rotation-event: key_id=ak_live_72efc rotated_by=maria.console user=acct-acmehealth timestamp=2026-03-14T12:20:13Z invalidation_published=true affected_regions=[eu,us-west]
ken (Infra): invalidation_published=true, but that doesn't guarantee immediate local flush. Which edge partition is returning connection refused? ben — can you grep for `eu-edge-3`?
ben (SRE): grepping now. Found consistent 401 spikes from `eu-edge-3` between 12:21:00–12:24:00 and a follow-up 503 window 12:22:30–12:23:10. Stack from envoy shows:

```
[envoy][error] upstream connect error or disconnect. iter=3 last_error=\"connection reset by peer\"
auth-service: 401 invalid api key id mismatch expected=ak_live_72efc got=ak_live_5f2b
```

ben (SRE): So some upstream auth pods still validating against the old key id (ak_live_5f2b) even after invalidation.
sophia (CSE): Customer is on Dedicated Reserved -> but using hosted control plane for key management. They are worried about client replays and downtime. They asked for a temporary rollback if needed.
jason (Eng): Two hypotheses: 1) Control plane published invalidation but the auth-service env var or mounted secret wasn't rotated on some auth pods (secret mount race). 2) There was a partial rollout of the auth-service with an older config due to a canary lock, causing mixed validators.
maria (Support): I asked AcmeHealth to hold off further key rotations. They also confirmed some clients do exponential backoff which makes the pattern messy.
ken (Infra): Steps I'm doing now:
- rolling restart of auth-service pods in eu-edge partition (graceful) to force secret reload
- forcing cache purge via admin endpoint `/admin/cache/purge?key_id=ak_live_5f2b`
- check Vault approle propagation: `vault read secret/data/apikeys/ak_live_72efc`
jason (Eng): Also check our KMS rewrap logs. If the new secret was encrypted under a different key version maybe some nodes can't unwrap.
ben (SRE): I initiated the rollout restart at 12:37 UTC. Early telemetry shows 401 rate coming down on eu-edge-3. Will watch for 10m.
maria (Support): Customer reported partial recovery at 12:42 UTC — traffic looks normal for them now. They asked what caused it and how to prevent in future.
jason (Eng): Root cause candidate: secret propagation race + sticky envoy connections to auth pods with stale validator config. Prevention: make rotation flow push an explicit hot-swap header and have edge proxies attempt handshake with both old+new key for a short overlap window (configurable grace). Also improve invalidation fanout (confirm ACKs from all edge nodes).
ken (Infra): Short-term mitigations we executed: forced restart, cache purge, confirm vault decrypts on all auth pods. Medium-term: decrease cache TTL from 5m to 1m for keys flagged rotating, and emit per-node ack on invalidation.
maria (Support): Customer accepted those mitigations and wants a post-incident note. They also requested a playbook for them: what to expect when rotating a key and how to do a staged rotation for critical clients.
sophia (CSE): I'll draft the customer-facing runbook and include recommended cadence: rotate during low-traffic window, coordinate with SRE for manual invalidation if they use client-side pinned proxies. Also recommend client backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd.
jason (Eng): Action items:
- [jason] add dual-key validation overlap (2h) as feature flag for rotations
- [ken] implement invalidation ACKs + per-node status metric
- [ben] create a k8s job to verify vault unwrap on all auth-service pods after rotation
- [sophia] customer runbook + postmortem summary
maria (Support): Thanks all. I'll send a summary to AcmeHealth with the timeline and the interim mitigations. Tagging this thread for postmortem once we have logs: @ben @ken @jason @sophia
